---
name: try-omarchy-linux
description: >-
  Use to install, launch, recover, or safely operate the Try Omarchy Flatpak VM
  (Omarchy desktop in a window) on a Linux computer, including one with no
  working KVM or one that gets reset.
---
# Try Omarchy on Linux

Try Omarchy runs the Omarchy desktop (Arch + Hyprland) as a QEMU VM inside a Flatpak app. Official page: https://tryomarchy.com/linux/

## Install
1. Make sure Flatpak is installed and Flathub is added (the runtime comes from Flathub):
   `flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists flathub https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo`
2. Download the app ref and install it per user:
   `curl -LO https://tryomarchy.com/linux.flatpakref`
   `flatpak install --user -y ./linux.flatpakref`
   This adds the `try-omarchy` remote (https://flatpak.tryomarchy.com/repo/) and installs `com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy` plus the GNOME runtime.
3. Verify: `flatpak info --user com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy`

## Decide KVM vs software emulation
- On a normal Linux PC with working `/dev/kvm`, just run `flatpak run com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy`.
- On a cloud VM or bot computer (nested virtualisation), KVM may be missing or may crash the host kernel. Unless the owner has confirmed KVM is safe, use software emulation (TCG) via the wrapper below. Never test KVM by just trying it on a shared machine.
- The app's preflight check refuses to start unless the user is in the group that owns `/dev/kvm`, even with the wrapper. Being in the group is fine as long as every launch goes through the wrapper.

## Software-emulation wrapper
Save as `~/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data/qemu-tcg-wrapper.sh` (inside the app's data dir so the sandbox can see it) and `chmod +x` it:
```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Rewrite the app's QEMU args to use TCG instead of KVM.
LOG="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data}/try-omarchy/vm/tcg-wrapper.log"
n=$#; i=0; prev=
while [ $i -lt $n ]; do
  a=$1; shift; i=$((i+1))
  case "$prev" in
    -machine|-M) a=$(printf '%s' "$a" | sed 's/accel=kvm/accel=tcg/');;
    -cpu) [ "$a" = host ] && a=max;;
  esac
  case "$a" in -enable-kvm|--enable-kvm) prev=$a; continue;; esac
  set -- "$@" "$a"; prev=$a
done
{ date; printf '%s\n' "args: $*"; } >> "$LOG" 2>/dev/null
exec /app/bin/qemu-system-x86_64 "$@"
```
Launch with:
`flatpak run com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy -qemu ~/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data/qemu-tcg-wrapper.sh -audio none`
The first run downloads and sets up the guest. After that it boots by itself in about 3 to 5 minutes. If the window stays black, relaunch with `-render cpu` added. Check that `tcg-wrapper.log` shows `accel=tcg`.

## Computers that get reset (restore script)
Some bot computers are rebuilt from a fresh image while the home folder is kept. The VM disk and app survive, but system pieces vanish: the `flatpak` package, the `kvm` group, and empty folders in the Flatpak runtime (bwrap then fails with "Can't create file /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/GL"). Save this as `~/bin/omarchy-box-restore.sh`, `chmod +x` it, and run it with `--launch` instead of launching by hand:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Restore what Try Omarchy needs after a reset; optionally launch via the TCG wrapper.
set -u
APP=com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy; DATA=$HOME/.var/app/$APP/data; WRAP=$DATA/qemu-tcg-wrapper.sh
log(){ echo "[restore] $*"; }
if ! command -v flatpak >/dev/null; then
  sudo apt-get update -q >/dev/null
  sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold flatpak </dev/null >/dev/null || { log "flatpak install FAILED"; exit 1; }
fi
sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive dpkg --force-confold --configure -a </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
name=
if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
  gid=$(stat -c %g /dev/kvm); name=$(getent group "$gid" | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$name" ] && sudo groupadd -g "$gid" kvm && name=kvm
  id -nG "$USER" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx "$name" || sudo usermod -aG "$name" "$USER"
fi
RT=$(flatpak --user info --show-runtime $APP 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$RT" ] && [ ! -d "$HOME/.local/share/flatpak/runtime/$RT/active/files/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/GL" ]; then
  log "repairing runtime $RT"; flatpak --user install --reinstall -y --noninteractive flathub "runtime/$RT" >/dev/null
fi
[ -x "$WRAP" ] || { log "TCG wrapper missing; refusing"; exit 1; }
log "system restore OK"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--launch" ]; then
  if pgrep -f qemu-system >/dev/null || pgrep -x try-omarchy >/dev/null; then log "already running; not launching"; exit 2; fi
  nohup sg "${name:-$(id -gn)}" -c "flatpak run --no-documents-portal $APP -qemu $WRAP -audio none ${EXTRA_ARGS:-}" > /tmp/try-omarchy-launch.log 2>&1 &
  sleep 30; pgrep -af qemu-system | grep -q accel=tcg && log "VM booting under TCG" || { log "did not start under TCG"; tail -3 /tmp/try-omarchy-launch.log; exit 3; }
fi
```
The script needs passwordless sudo. Ask the owner before letting it create or join the `kvm` group the first time, because once the account is in that group, launching without the wrapper would use KVM.

## Safety rules
- Before launching, check it isn't already running: `pgrep -f qemu-system` and `pgrep -x try-omarchy`. Never run two instances on the same disk image, because that can corrupt it. If another session or bot has it open, ask them to shut it down cleanly (`sudo poweroff` in the guest) rather than killing QEMU.
- VM data lives in `~/.var/app/com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy/data/try-omarchy/vm/`. Never delete `disk.raw`.
- To stop a stuck guest cleanly from the host, send `kill -INT` to the `try-omarchy` process, which asks the guest to power off. Don't kill QEMU directly.

## Common errors
- "this account is not allowed to use KVM": the group is missing. Run the restore script.
- "Can't find source path ~/.cache/doc/...": a stale documents portal. Launch with `--no-documents-portal`.
- "already running, or another program is using its port 4450": an old `try-omarchy` process, often a leftover error dialog, is still running.
- "X connection ... broken" in `qemu-stderr.log`: the host display went away and took the VM with it. Relaunch.

## Using the guest
- Default login is `omarchy` / `omarchy`, and sudo doesn't ask for a password.
- Super+Space opens the Omarchy menu, Super+Enter opens a terminal, Super+K shows the keybindings, and Super+W closes a window. Ctrl+Alt+G releases the keyboard grab back to the host.
- Install a theme with `omarchy theme install <git-url>`, then pick it under Super+Space > Style > Theme. Install doesn't apply it automatically.
- Shell plugins (`omarchy plugin add ...`) need the Quattro omarchy-shell. If they fail with "omarchy-shell is not responding", move the guest to the dev channel with `omarchy-channel-set dev` (a long update), then run `omarchy-migrate`.
- Emulation is slow, so wait for screens to settle before each action and verify with screenshots.

---
name: omarchy-operator-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation for an Omarchy operator bot with its new owner: learn their
  setup, then install and launch Try Omarchy.
---
# Getting started (Omarchy operator)

You run tasks inside Omarchy (DHH's Arch + Hyprland desktop) using the Try Omarchy VM on your computer, following the try-omarchy-linux skill.

Open with a short hello, then ask one question at a time:
1. "Should I set up Try Omarchy on my computer now, or is it already installed?" Check with `flatpak info --user com.tryomarchy.TryOmarchy` and `pgrep -f qemu-system` before assuming.
2. "Is KVM safe to use on this machine?" If they don't know, or it's a bot or cloud computer, default to the software-emulation wrapper. Never just try KVM to find out.
3. "Do any of your other bots also use this VM?" If so, agree that only one runs at a time and the other closes it first.
4. "What would you like me to do first?" Examples are a theme, a package, a plugin, or a config tweak.

Then:
- Save the answers as memories (KVM decision, launch command, who else uses the VM).
- Install if needed. On a bot or cloud computer, also save the restore script from try-omarchy-linux and launch with it from then on, so a computer reset doesn't break the VM. Otherwise launch per try-omarchy-linux. Warn that it boots in a few minutes.
- Send a screenshot once the Omarchy desktop is up, then start on their first task.
